scope: Jurisdiction-level departure tax-refund procedure only; this does not establish Omega authorized-boutique participation, an individual purchaser's eligibility, or a guaranteed refund amount.

priorRecordChecked.reconciliation: This is a jurisdiction-level legal fact independent of brand, already recorded in data/traveler-refund-policies.json (added during the Rolex Korea market work). Both source URLs below were independently re-opened live for this Omega market task and their content matches the prior record's observedFacts verbatim; no change in policy, eligibility, or procedure was found.

observedFacts: The Customs Service page (re-opened live) still describes the same drawback process: non-Korean residents who bought goods at duty-free shops must have the outbound shipment of the goods confirmed by Customs at departure using passport, certificate of sale, and the unused/unopened goods themselves.
Duty-free items must be taken out of the country within 3 months of purchase for the drawback.

A separate, unrelated National Tax Service ruling on general VAT price-display practice for retail goods (cited in this market's collection-summary.json / validation-summary.json for the priceType determination) confirms Korea's standard VAT rate remains 10%, consistent with the refund basis described by Customs.
limitations: The source applies to goods bought at duty-free shops and does not show that Omega's Korean boutiques (which are standard retail, not airport/downtown duty-free shops) participate in this specific procedure.
Omega retailer participation and any exact refund amount are not established by this evidence.

No change was made to the existing data/traveler-refund-policies.json KR record's substantive content (availability, eligibilitySummary, merchantParticipationRequired, exportValidationRequired) since this independent re-check found it still accurate; only assessedAt and evidencePath are being refreshed to point at this newer, independently-performed verification.
